title: A Guide to Moving to Dallas: Big Energy, Bright Futures, and Living in North Texas
summary: Thinking about moving to Dallas, TX? Discover top job markets, world-class arts, top-rated school districts, and new construction home opportunities in North Texas.
body_text: Posted by Chandler Wall in Dallas , Local Guides and Resources ) From a booming economic hub to a rich cultural landscape, Dallas, Texas has quickly become a premier choice for people seeking vibrant living in the heart of North Texas. Whether you are relocating for expanding career opportunities, seeking top-tier school districts, or simply wanting a fresh chapter in a fast-moving metropolitan region, the Big D delivers an incredible lifestyle. Offering a perfect mix of modern urban energy, classic Southern charm, and booming suburban destinations, living in Dallas provides endless convenience and growth. It’s no surprise that so many families and professionals are choosing to set down roots here. If you're considering moving to Dallas, Texas, explore what makes this dynamic market such an outstanding location to call home! A Flourishing Economy and Job Market The Dallas-Fort Worth region features one of the most robust and diverse economies in the nation. Recognized globally as a powerhouse for commerce, technology, finance, and healthcare, the area continues to attract major corporate headquarters and innovative startups alike. Notable major employers and industry hubs in the area include: Telecom Corridor & Tech Hubs : Home to major operations for global technology leaders like Texas Instruments, Ericsson, and AT&T. Financial & Corporate Leaders : Regional headquarters for powerhouse brands such as Charles Schwab, Southwest Airlines , and Toyota Motor North America. Healthcare Networks : Leading research and clinical systems, including UT Southwestern Medical Center and Baylor Scott & White Health. With a thriving business climate and steady job creation across every sector, Dallas offers an ideal environment for long-term career growth. Rich Culture, Entertainment, and Dining Life in Dallas comes with access to world-class arts, sports, and a legendary food scene. The iconic Dallas Arts District stands as the largest continuous urban arts district in the country, spanning 20 square blocks of museums, performance halls, and stunning architecture. Local cultural and entertainment highlights include: Dallas Museum of Art : Featuring expansive global art collections alongside interactive exhibitions for visitors of all ages. Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden : A 66-acre oasis situated along White Rock Lake, famous for seasonal floral festivals and scenic walking paths. Klyde Warren Park : A lively deck park built over a freeway, featuring daily food trucks, outdoor fitness classes, and family-friendly lawns. Food lovers will appreciate the region's incredible culinary diversity, from iconic Tex-Mex joints and upscale steak houses to vibrant dining hotspots throughout Deep Ellum and Trinity Groves. Sports enthusiasts can also catch top-tier professional action year-round with the Dallas Cowboys, Dallas Mavericks, Dallas Stars, and Texas Rangers. Outdoor Recreation and Scenic Green Spaces Despite its impressive skyline, Dallas offers plenty of picturesque outdoor spaces for nature lovers and active individuals. Warm sunshine and accessible park systems make outdoor recreation a daily perk. Popular local green spaces include: White Rock Lake : A massive urban lake featuring over nine miles of hiking and biking trails, kayak rentals, and scenic sunset views. The Katy Trail : A historic 3.5-mile rail-trail winding through Uptown and Oak Lawn, ideal for walking, running, and cycling. Cedar Hill State Park : Located just a short drive away, offering miles of rugged mountain bike trails and quiet lake views along Joe Pool Lake. Outstanding Educational Opportunities For families considering a move to Dallas, education is a top priority. The region boasts several highly sought-after public school systems across its flourishing suburban communities, including the nationally recognized Frisco ISD and Prosper ISD . Higher education is equally prestigious in the North Texas area, anchored by renowned institutions like Southern Methodist University (SMU) and the University of Texas at Dallas (UTD), bringing incredible research talent and cultural energy to the metroplex. Discover New Construction Opportunities in Dallas With its high energy, booming job prospects, and outstanding quality of life, moving to Dallas is an exciting step forward. Whether you want to stay connected to urban centers or settle into a quiet neighborhood setting, North Texas has something tailored for every lifestyle. If you're ready to start your journey, explore our newly constructed single-story designs today! Every plan features functional living layouts with the owner's suite tucked away in its own private corner, giving you the perfect retreat to relax and recharge. title: CME Group to Expand Retail Access to Four Leading Benchmarks with E-nano Equity Index Futures Launch on August 24
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about CME Group Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Contracts will be one-tenth the size of Micro E-mini futures for S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, Russell 2000 and Dow Jones Industrial Average CHICAGO , Aug. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CME Group, the world's leading derivatives marketplace, today announced plans to expand its smaller-sized contract suite with the launch of E-nano equity index futures on August 24, pending regulatory review. At one-tenth the size of Micro E-mini futures, these new nano-sized contracts are designed to enable institutional and retail investors to optimize exposure to the market's leading equity benchmarks. Clients can express views on the S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, Russell 2000 and Dow Jones Industrial Average 23 hours per day, with additional precision for risk management strategies. "As equity markets continue to reach all-time highs, the barrier to entry has increased for retail investors, creating a need for even smaller contracts that deliver cost efficiency and enhanced flexibility," said Tim McCourt, Global Head of Equities, FX and Alternative Products at CME Group. "E-nano equity index futures will enable our clients to hedge their portfolios with an unprecedented level of granularity, all within the trusted infrastructure and centralized liquidity that is available from CME Group." "U.S. equity markets have been on a historic run, and that's great news for investors; however, they're operating without the benefits that futures uniquely provide, such as capital efficiency, margin offsets and nearly 23-hour access to trade macro events as they unfold," said Martin Franchi, CEO, NinjaTrader Group. "Nano-sized equity futures through CME Group change that calculus. We see this as another significant expansion of access to U.S. equity futures, and NinjaTrader is proud to bring it to our community." "Launching nano-sized equity index futures later this summer is another key milestone in Robinhood's mission to democratize access for all," said JB Mackenzie, VP and GM of Futures and Prediction Markets at Robinhood. "As major US equity benchmarks climb to historic highs, some retail traders are being priced out of existing futures products. We're excited to work with CME Group to make it even easier for customers to trade these benchmarks with contracts that are one tenth the size of what's available today." Since launching in May 2019, approximately 4.5 billion Micro E-mini futures have traded at CME Group. With demand for smaller-sized equity index futures growing in recent years, the complex is seeing record levels of volume and participation, including: Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures – record monthly ADV of 3.2 million contracts in June Micro E-mini S&P 500 futures – record quarterly ADV of 1.5 million contracts in Q1 E-nano equity index futures will be listed on and subject to the rules of CME and CBOT. For more information on these products, please visit cmegroup.com/enano . As the world's leading derivatives marketplace, CME Group ( www.cmegroup.com ) enables clients to trade futures, options, cash and OTC markets, optimize portfolios, and analyze data – empowering market participants worldwide to efficiently manage risk and capture opportunities. CME Group exchanges offer the widest range of global benchmark products across all major asset classes based on interest rates , equity indexes , foreign exchange , cryptocurrencies , energy , agricultural products and metals . The company offers futures and options on futures trading through the CME Globex platform, fixed income trading via BrokerTec and foreign exchange trading on the EBS platform. In addition, it operates one of the world's leading central counterparty clearing providers, CME Clearing. title: West Nile Virus Cases Rise Across the US as Drought Creates New Mosquito Risks

body_text: A mosquito-borne illness that can cause severe inflammation of the brain and spinal cord is spreading across parts of the United States, with health officials warning people to take extra precautions during the summer months. West Nile virus has been detected in at least 30 US states so far this year, with more than 180 human cases recorded nationally, according to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) . At least eight people have died. Arizona has reported the highest number of cases, with 73 infections and five deaths. California has also experienced a notable rise, reporting 30 human cases and three deaths, according to state health data. That figure is around three times the number recorded in the state at the same point last year. The increase is particularly concerning because severe West Nile infections can cause neurological complications. While many people who contract the virus experience no symptoms or develop only mild illness, a small proportion can become seriously ill. A virus that can affect the brain West Nile virus is mainly transmitted through the bite of an infected mosquito. Mosquitoes become infected after feeding on birds carrying the virus and can then pass it to humans and other animals. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention , most people infected with West Nile virus do not develop symptoms. Others may experience fever, headache, body aches, vomiting, skin rashes or swollen lymph glands. The more serious form of the disease, known as West Nile neuroinvasive disease, can cause inflammation of the brain or the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord. Symptoms can include a high fever, confusion, tremors, muscle weakness, vision problems, paralysis and, in the most serious cases, coma or death. There is currently no specific antiviral treatment or vaccine for people infected with West Nile virus. Medical care generally focuses on managing symptoms and supporting patients while their bodies fight the infection. Older adults and people with weakened immune systems are among those at greater risk of developing severe disease. California sees a significant increase California has become one of the states attracting particular attention this summer. State figures show 30 human cases so far in 2026, including three deaths. Few details have been released publicly about the deaths, although local health authorities said at least one person was aged between 80 and 90 and died following complications associated with the infection. The rise in cases has also affected individual communities. In Elk Grove, California, a 70-year-old man was recently hospitalised after developing a serious illness associated with West Nile virus. According to ABC10 , the patient underwent a spinal tap as doctors investigated his condition. A member of his family, Jeanetta McDowell, urged people to take mosquito protection seriously. Her advice was simple: use insect repellent, cover exposed skin and take steps to reduce the risk of mosquito bites. Idaho reports severe disease California is not the only state to have recorded serious infections. Idaho has reported its first severe West Nile virus case of the season. The patient is a 65-year-old resident of Canyon County who developed meningitis linked to the virus. The Idaho Department of Health and Welfare said the case should serve as a reminder that people need to protect themselves from mosquito bites. Dr Christine Hahn, Idaho's state epidemiologist, encouraged residents to take preventative measures during the mosquito season. West Nile virus is not a new threat in the US. The infection causes more than 130 deaths in the contiguous United States in an average year, demonstrating that severe disease can occur even though most infections are relatively mild. Why drought may be making the problem worse The spread of West Nile virus might appear surprising in areas experiencing drought. Mosquitoes generally need water to reproduce, so it could be assumed that dry conditions would reduce mosquito populations. Scientists say the reality is more complicated. In parts of the western US, drought can create conditions that increase the risk of West Nile transmission. As larger bodies of water shrink, mosquitoes and birds can become concentrated around the remaining sources of water. That closer proximity can create more opportunities for the virus to move between infected birds and mosquitoes. Matthew Aliota, a professor at the University of Minnesota who studies viruses transmitted by mosquitoes and other vectors, previously explained the phenomenon to The Independent . According to Aliota, drought can paradoxically increase transmission by concentrating mosquitoes and birds around shrinking water sources. This year, the US has experienced significant drought across parts of the country. CNN reported earlier this year that historic drought conditions contributed to major wildfires and record-low snowpack in some regions. The effects, however, are not uniform across the country. Some states have seen mosquito activity below normal levels. Colorado, North Dakota and Minnesota are among the areas where mosquito numbers have been lower than usual this summer. How people can protect themselves Health officials say individuals can take several straightforward steps to reduce their exposure to mosquitoes. The most important measures include using insect repellent when spending time outdoors and wearing clothing that covers the arms and legs. People should also check around their homes for standing water. Mosquitoes can lay eggs in surprisingly small amounts of water. Containers, buckets, plant pots, blocked drains and other objects that collect rainwater can therefore become potential breeding sites. Removing standing water regularly can help reduce the number of mosquitoes around homes and gardens. The Idaho Department of Health and Welfare recommends combining personal protection with efforts to reduce mosquito breeding areas. For people living in areas where West Nile virus is circulating, these precautions are particularly important during the warmer months, when mosquito activity generally reaches its highest levels. A growing seasonal concern West Nile virus remains a seasonal public health concern in the United States, but the latest figures highlight how environmental conditions can influence the spread of mosquito-borne diseases. The situation also demonstrates why lower mosquito numbers do not necessarily mean lower infection risk. In drought-affected areas, changes in water availability can alter the behaviour and concentration of mosquitoes and birds, potentially creating conditions that favour transmission. For most people, infection will not result in serious illness. However, the possibility of neurological disease, hospitalisation and death means that prevention remains important. As summer continues, health authorities are urging residents to avoid mosquito bites wherever possible, remove standing water around their homes and seek medical advice if they develop concerning symptoms after spending time in areas where West Nile virus has been detected. The message from public health officials is straightforward: mosquito bites may seem like a minor nuisance, but the virus they can carry can have serious consequences. Sources Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) California West Nile Virus and Mosquito-Borne Disease Information Idaho Department of Health and Welfare ABC10 CNN The Independent

title: Kingsoft Cloud Announces Unaudited Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: BEIJING, Aug. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kingsoft Cloud Holdings Limited (" Kingsoft Cloud " or the "Company") (NASDAQ: KC and HKEX: 3896), a leading cloud service provider in China, today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Mr.
body_text: BEIJING , Aug. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kingsoft Cloud Holdings Limited ("Kingsoft Cloud" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: KC and HKEX: 3896), a leading cloud service provider in China, today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Mr. Tao Zou, Chief Executive Officer of Kingsoft Cloud, commented: "We are excited to deliver a quarter of both strong growth and profitability. Gross billings from our AI cloud business grew 82% year-over-year, representing 56% of public cloud revenue, driven by incremental contributions from our AI cloud infrastructure services as well as Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) offerings. Profitability-wise, we recorded positive operating margin (GAAP) for the first time, and our adjusted operating profit margin increased significantly to reach 4.0% [ 1] , thanks to our improved gross margin and operating efficiency. We remain committed to pursuing high-quality, sustainable growth strategy, deepening collaboration with customers both within and beyond our ecosystem, and strengthening our market position." Ms. Yi Li, Chief Financial Officer of Kingsoft Cloud, added, "We delivered a strong quarter, with total revenue reaching a record high of RMB3,072.0 million, representing an increase of 30.8% year-over-year. Adjusted gross profit increased by 34.6% year-over-year to RMB471.7 million, with an adjusted gross margin of 15.4% [ 2] , an improvement from last quarter. We also reached breakeven on operating profit (GAAP), with adjusted operating profit margin reaching 4.0%, demonstrating improving profitability thanks to AI demand tailwinds and operational optimization. We remain committed to investing for sustainable long-term growth, with capital expenditures (including capitalized assets through leasing arrangements) amounting to RMB3.3 billion in Q2, an increase from Q1." S econd Quarter 2026 Financial Results Total Revenues reached RMB3,072.0 million (US$452.8 [ 3] million), increased by 30.8% year-over-year from RMB2,349.2 million in the same quarter of 2025, and increased by 13.6% quarter-over-quarter from RMB2,703.7 million in the first quarter of 2026. The increase was mainly due to revenue growth from AI-related customers, supported by continued upgrades to our AI infrastructure and product offerings. Revenues from public cloud services were RMB2,357.6 million (US$347.5 million), increased by 45.1% year-over-year from RMB1,625.3 million in the same quarter of 2025 and increased by 18.1% quarter-over-quarter from RMB1,996.3 million last quarter. The increase was mainly driven by growing demand for AI cloud services. AI cloud gross billings reached RMB1,327 million (US$195.6 million), while our other public cloud services also maintained solid growth. Revenues from enterprise cloud services were RMB714.3 million (US$105.3 million), representing a year-over-year decrease of 1.3% from RMB723.9 million in the same quarter of 2025 and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 1.0% from RMB707.4 million last quarter. [1] Our operating profit margin was 0.7%. [2] Our gross profit was RMB466.2 million, representing a year-over-year increase of 37.6%, with a gross margin of 15.2%. [3] This announcement contains translations of certain Renminbi (RMB) amounts into U.S. dollars (US$) at a specified rate solely for the convenience of the reader. Unless otherwise noted, the translation of RMB into US$ has been made at RMB6.7851 to US$1.00, the noon buying rate in effect on June 30, 2026 as certified for customs purposes by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Cost of revenues was RMB2,605.8 million (US$384.0 million), representing an increase of 29.6% from RMB2,010.4 million in the same quarter of 2025, which was mainly due to our continued investment in AI computing resources. IDC costs increased by 23.3% year-over-year from RMB803.1 million to RMB990.1 million (US$146.0 million) this quarter, largely in line with our revenue expansion. Depreciation and amortization costs increased from RMB552.0 million in the same quarter of 2025 to RMB963.8 million (US$142.0 million) this quarter. The increase was mainly due to the depreciation of newly acquired and leased servers, and network equipment which were mainly related to AI cloud business. Solution development and services costs increased by 3.9% year-over-year from RMB563.7 million in the same quarter of 2025 to RMB585.7 million (US$86.3 million) this quarter. The increase was mainly due to the solution personnel expansion. Fulfillment costs and other costs were RMB15.1 million (US$2.2 million) and RMB51.1 million (US$7.5 million) this quarter. Gross profit was RMB466.2 million (US$68.7 million), representing an increase of 37.6% from RMB338.9 million in the same quarter of 2025. The increase was mainly due to the expansion of our revenue scale, especially the intelligent computing services. Gross margin was 15.2% in this quarter, compared with 14.4% in the same quarter of 2025 and 12.8% last quarter. The increase was mainly due to higher profit contribution from our AI cloud business. Non-GAAP gross profit [ 4] was RMB471.7 million (US$69.5 million), compared with RMB350.6 million in the same period in 2025. Non-GAAP gross margin [ 4] was 15.4%, compared with 14.9% in the same period in 2025. Total operating expenses were RMB443.2 million (US$65.3 million), decreased by 33.4% from RMB665.8 million in the same quarter of 2025 and decreased by 13.4% from RMB511.9 million last quarter. Among which: Selling and marketing expenses were RMB113.1 million (US$16.7 million), decreased by 14.3% from RMB132.0 million in the same period in 2025 and decreased by 8.6% from RMB123.8 million last quarter. The decrease was mainly due to the decrease of share-based compensation and personnel costs. General and administrative expenses were RMB140.2 million (US$20.6 million), decreased by 58.7% from RMB339.6 million in the same period in 2025 and decreased by 28.0% from RMB194.8 million last quarter. The decrease was mainly due to the decrease of credit loss expenses and share-based compensation. Research and development expenses were RMB189.9 million (US$28.0 million), decreased by 2.3% from RMB194.3 million in the same period in 2025 and decreased by 1.8% from RMB193.3 million last quarter. The year-over-year decrease was mainly due to the decrease of personnel costs and share-based compensation. Operating profit was RMB23.0 million (US$3.4 million), compared with operating loss of RMB327.0 million in the same period in 2025 and operating loss of RMB166.1 million last quarter. The year-over-year improvement was mainly due to the increase of revenue, while the sequential improvement was mainly due to the impact of increase in gross profit. Non-GAAP operating profit [5] was RMB124.0 million (US$18.3 million), compared with operating loss of RMB166.4 million in the same period last year and operating loss of RMB59.8 million last quarter. [4] Non-GAAP gross profit is defined as gross profit excluding share-based compensation expenses allocated in the cost of revenues and we define Non-GAAP gross margin as Non-GAAP gross profit as a percentage of revenues. See "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" set forth at the end of this press release. [5] Non-GAAP operating (loss) profit is defined as operating (loss) profit excluding share-based compensation expenses and amortization of intangible assets and we define Non-GAAP operating (loss) profit margin as Non-GAAP operating (loss) profit as a percentage of revenues. See "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" set forth at the end of this press release. Net loss was RMB93.0 million (US$13.7 million), narrowed by 79.6% from RMB456.9 million in the same quarter of 2025 and narrowed by 72.9% from RMB343.7 million last quarter. Non-GAAP net loss [ 6] was RMB59.8 million (US$8.8 million), compared with RMB300.5 million in the same quarter of 2025 and RMB237.1 million last quarter. Non-GAAP EBITDA [7] was RMB1,100.5 million (US$162.2 million), compared with RMB406.0 million in the same quarter of 2025 and RMB747.5 million last quarter. Non-GAAP EBITDA margin was 35.8%, compared with 17.3% in the same quarter of 2025 and 27.6% last quarter. Basic and diluted net loss per share was RMB0.02 (US$0.00), compared with RMB0.11 in the same quarter of 2025 and RMB0.08 last quarter. Cash and cash equivalents were RMB4,674.3 million (US$688.9 million) as of June 30, 2026, compared with RMB6,018.0 million as of December 31, 2025. The decrease was mainly due to the investment into the procurement of computing power equipment. Outstanding ordinary shares were 4,501,784,337 as of June 30, 2026, equivalent to about 300,118,956 ADSs. summary: Second quarter of 2026 revenue increased 62.3% year-over-year to $9.3 million Second-quarter bookings reached $15.1 million, representing the highest quarterly bookings in the Company’s history Company raises full year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 25% to 30% ESCONDIDO, Calif. – August 5, 2026 – One Stop Systems, Inc. (
body_text: Second quarter of 2026 revenue increased 62.3% year-over-year to $9.3 million Second-quarter bookings reached $15.1 million, representing the highest quarterly bookings in the Company’s history Company raises full year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 25% to 30% ESCONDIDO, Calif. – August 5, 2026 – One Stop Systems, Inc. ("OSS" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: OSS), a leader in rugged Enterprise Class compute for artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), autonomy and sensor processing at the edge, reported results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Second-quarter and six-month comparisons are to the same year-ago periods unless otherwise noted. On December 30, 2025, the Company closed a definitive agreement to sell all assets and operations of Bressner Technology GmbH. All operations, assets, and liabilities associated with the sale of Bressner have been classified as discontinued operations. “OSS delivered another quarter of strong year-over-year revenue growth, which accelerated to 62.3% in the second quarter from 55.0% in the first quarter, reflecting continued execution against our multi-year strategic plan and growing demand for rugged, enterprise-class compute at the edge,” stated OSS President and CEO, Mike Knowles. “I am pleased to report that we also achieved the strongest quarterly bookings results in our history, with second quarter bookings reaching $15.1 million. This produced a book-to-bill ratio of 1.6x for the quarter and 1.7x year-to-date, which we believe provides strong support for continued growth. Our year-to-date results have benefited from important program-of-record activity, including a new intelligence platform for the U.S. Department of Defense that is expected to generate approximately $44 million over the next four years.” “Our momentum also reflects a growing portion of revenue and bookings generated across an increasingly diverse range of defense and commercial customers. This includes mission-critical defense applications across C5ISR, sensor fusion, and autonomy programs serving both defense and commercial markets, and niche data center, robotics and medical applications. Many of these opportunities originated as development initiatives over the past several years and are now increasingly transitioning into larger scale, multi-year production orders. We believe this broadening activity demonstrates that OSS is gaining market share and becoming an increasingly important technology partner for organizations that require enterprise-class compute in demanding and rugged environments,” continued, Mr. Knowles. “Given our strong start to the year, continued bookings momentum and expanding program activity, we are increasing our full-year revenue guidance. Overall, we believe OSS is well positioned to deliver sustained growth and create meaningful long-term shareholder value for years to come,” concluded Mr. Knowles. 2026 Second-Quarter Financial Summary Total revenue from continuing operations increased 62.3% to $9.3 million, from $5.8 million in the second quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher sales to a medical imaging OEM of liquid-cooled server products to support a breast cancer screening application, as the customer moved from initial prototypes in 2025 to production in 2026; sales with a new customer for short-depth server products engineered for military applications onboard naval vessels and aircraft; and sales with a new customer for compute products to support autonomous construction and mining equipment. Gross margin from continuing operations was 39.1% for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to 41.3% in the prior year quarter. The decrease in gross margin was primarily driven by product mix, including a higher level of customer-funded development, early prototype and low-rate initial production activities, partially offset by more favorable manufacturing absorption due to higher production volume and higher usage of reserved inventory to fulfill customer orders. During the second quarter of 2026, OSS recorded a $6.25 million charge related to the settlement of a legacy commercial dispute involving a former customer relationship and events dating back several years ago. The one-time settlement does not constitute an admission of liability, is unrelated to the Company’s current operations or growth programs and fully resolves the dispute. Total operating expenses from continuing operations increased 129.8% to $11.3 million, and included a $6.25 million legal settlement charge described above. Excluding the legal settlement, total operating expenses from continuing operations increased 2.9% to $5.1 million. This increase was predominantly attributable to higher general and administrative and marketing and selling expenses and partially offset by lower R&D expenses. The Company reported a loss from continuing operations of $7.3 million, or $0.29 per diluted share for the three months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to a loss from continuing operations of $2.5 million, or $0.11 per share, in the prior year period. The Company reported a non-GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $0.2 million, or $0.01 per diluted share, compared to a non-GAAP net loss of $2.0 million, or $0.09 per share, in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA loss, from continuing operations, a non-GAAP metric, was $0.3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to an adjusted EBITDA loss, from continuing operations, of $1.8 million in the prior year period. Net cash used in continuing operations for the six months ended June 30, 2026, was $0.6 million, compared to net cash used in continuing operations of $2.8 million in the prior year period. As of June 30, 2026, the Company reported cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of $ 31.4 million, and total working capital of $ 38.1 million, compared to cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of $31.2 million, restricted cash of $2.2 million and total working capital of $45.3 million at December 31, 2025. 2026 First-Half Financial Summary Total revenue from continuing operations increased 58.8% to $17.4 million, compared to $11.0 million for the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by revenue generated from new customers in 2026 and from higher production volume with certain existing customers. Gross margin from continuing operations was 44.9%, as compared to 43.3% in the prior year. The increase in gross margin percentage was primarily driven by engineering efficiencies realized on certain of our customer-funded development programs and more favorable manufacturing absorption due to higher production volume. Total operating expenses increased 67.5% to $16.2 million , and included a $6.25 million charge related to the legal settlement charge described above. Excluding the legal settlement, total operating expenses increased 2.7% to $9.9 million. This increase was predominantly attributable to higher personnel and professional services costs, offset by lower research and development expenses. OSS reported a loss from continuing operations of $7.7 million, or $0.31 per share, as compared to a loss from continuing operations of $4.8 million, or $0.22 per share, in the prior year. The Company reported non-GAAP net income from continuing operations of $0.1 million, or $0.00 per share, compared to a non-GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $3.7 million, or $0.17 per share in the prior year. Adjusted EBITDA loss, from continuing operations, a non-GAAP metric , was a loss of $0.2 million, compared to an adjusted EBITDA loss, from continuing operations, of $3.4 million in the prior year period. Income from Discontinued Operations, net of Income Taxes Income from discontinued operations consists of income from the Company’s Bressner Technologies subsidiary, which was sold on December 30, 2025. Income from discontinued operations also includes the gain recognized on the sale. The Company recorded no income or loss from discontinued operations, net of income taxes, for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to income of $0.5 million in the prior year. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, loss from discontinued operations, net of income taxes, was $0.2 million, compared to income from discontinued operations, net of income taxes, of $0.7 million in the prior year. The loss in the current year period was due to post-transaction adjustments to the gain on sale of the Bressner business for final net working capital balances. 2026 Full Year Outlook The Company is executing a strategic plan targeting both commercial and defense markets, aiming to provide integrated solutions and establish OSS as a platform incumbent on large, multi-year programs. This approach is expected to drive long-term value by increasing predictable, recurring revenue and building a strong, multi-year backlog. Based on its current performance and business outlook, OSS is increasing its full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance. The Company’s expectations for 2026 reflect expected continued growth across its core defense and commercial markets and expected higher customer-funded development revenue compared with 2025. The Company also continues to monitor potential supply chain constraints affecting certain components, including memory, and the current outlook for the federal government budget. Changes in these assumptions could positively or negatively affect OSS’s 2026 results. For the full year of 2026, OSS expects: - Revenue growth of 25% to 30%, compared to prior guidance of 20% to 25% - Gross margin of approximately 40% - Positive EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA, inclusive of planned strategic investments in personnel and research and development to support continued growth and technology leadership Conference Call OSS will hold a conference call to discuss its results for the second quarter of 2026, followed by a question-and-answer period. Don’t Dig Blind, Call 811
summary: Beneath the streets you drive every day, there is a hidden maze of gas, electric, water and fiber lines lurking. Most people never think about it, but for Theo Romero, it's ...
body_text: Beneath the streets you drive every day, there is a hidden maze of gas, electric, water and fiber lines lurking. Most people never think about it, but for Theo Romero, it’s constantly on his mind. Romero is a utility locate technician for UtiliQuest . His job is to find buried utility lines and mark them before projects break ground — work that starts with a free call to 811 . “You never know what you’re going to get,” Romero said. “It could be as small as planting some new trees or as large as trenching to install a storm drain. Either way, they need to call us first.” UtiliQuest locate technicians Theo Romero and Michael Serrano (l-r) mark the access point to a buried line. Administered by DigAlert in Southern California, calling 811 is a a free, required notification step every homeowner and contractor should make at least two working days before digging. DigAlert will then generate a ticket that will get assigned to a locator like Romero with UtiliQuest, who will go to the site with paint and flags, ready to mark underground utilities — electric, power, water, gas and sewer — so no one digs blind. One of his recent jobs sent him to Pomona, where the construction was more than a backyard home improvement project. “The dig here will impact the entire community,” said Romero. “There is going to be a new gas line installed which will support and connect the new homes currently under construction.” Utility line locating equipment traces the signal of a buried line, and then paint is used to mark its direction. The first thing his crew looks for is white — the color of paint or flags a homeowner or contractor uses to let Romero’s crew know where they plan to dig. “White marks are our bread and butter,” Romero said. “They show us exactly where the construction will take place, so we know the area to focus on.” From there, GPS maps show nearby structures and roughly where each line runs, along with when it was installed. But maps can be outdated or incorrect. “We need to know we’re in the right spot,” said Romero. “Sometimes the lines are not exactly where our maps say they will be, so we need to update that information” When that happens, the crew connects specialized equipment to the line, traces the signal and paints or plants flags in the ground, turning what’s invisible below ground into something anyone can see. UtiliQuest locator Theo Romero and his partner, Michael Serrano (l-r), trace the frequency of an underground utility line and mark it before crews begin construction. When someone skips the call to 811, it can lead to underground utility damage and serious consequences, including power outages, costly repairs, fines and safety hazards like explosions and fatal injuries. Even a small nick of a line can be disastrous. If it happens, stop digging immediately and call 811 so a professional can inspect the line before a minor problem becomes a major one. “Everyone should be using 811 before starting a project,” said Romero. “If you don’t, your whole project could be delayed for months, or worse, you could put yourself and your community at serious risk. There’s a whole team ready to help, just give us a call.” Tips For Before You Dig Call 811 or request a ticket online at least two working days ahead — it's free and required by law in the state of California. Outline your dig area with white paint, flags or chalk to help guide the locator. Be specific: When you or your contractor submit the ticket, describe exactly where the digging will take place. Wait until professionals mark the lines, then dig at least 24 inches away from them. Use hand tools when digging within 24 inches on each side of any marked utility lines. Dig with caution — lines can sit just inches below the surface. If you hit a line, even just a nick, stop digging and call 811 right away. If there is any gas leak, water leak or electrical discharge, leave the area and call 911 immediately. For more information, visit sce.com/safety .

title: Byrna Appoints Retired U.S. Army Brigadier General Rose Lopez Keravuori to Board of Directors
body_text: Byrna Appoints Retired U.S. Army Brigadier General Rose Lopez Keravuori to Board of Directors Download as PDF August 12, 2026 4:05pm EDT ANDOVER, Mass., Aug. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Byrna Technologies Inc. (“Byrna” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: BYRN), a personal defense technology company specializing in the development, manufacture, and sale of innovative less-lethal personal security solutions, today announced the appointment of retired U.S. Army Brigadier General Rose Lopez Keravuori to its Board of Directors (the “Board”), effective August 10, 2026. She has also been named, along with two other independent directors, Board Chair TJ Kennedy and Adam Roth, and CEO Conn Davis, to a newly formed Enterprise Risk Management Committee to assist the Board in its strategic oversight of risk management. Keravuori succeeds Emily Rooney, whose resignation from the Board became effective the same date. Keravuori brings more than three decades of leadership experience across strategic operations, crisis management, risk mitigation, and international affairs. Her experience reflects a unique combination of operational excellence, cultural diplomacy, and innovative problem-solving, making her well qualified to contribute to Board leadership and strategic oversight in support of the Company’s effort to strengthen performance, position the Company for long-term growth, and deliver sustainable shareholder returns. Keravuori served in the U.S. Army from 1997 until her retirement in 2025, most recently as director of intelligence for U.S. Africa Command. In that role, she served as a senior advisor to the commander, providing real-time intelligence and strategic guidance for critical operations while helping shape the command’s long-term priorities. Keravuori’s operational assignments included Germany, Kosovo, Afghanistan, Iraq, and Africa, where she led multinational security initiatives and supported crisis-response and risk-management efforts in complex environments. Throughout her distinguished military career, Keravuori commanded intelligence organizations, led large complex teams, and advised senior military and government leaders on national security, strategic planning, and international affairs. Keravuori’s private-sector experience includes leadership positions with BAE Systems, where she was responsible for business development, program management, and operations. She also founded and served as chief executive officer of ROSE Solutions, a consulting firm specializing in the development and implementation of strategic initiatives for clients ranging from small businesses to federal agencies. Keravuori is a graduate of the United States Military Academy at West Point and holds a Master of Studies in Diplomatic Studies from the University of Oxford, a Master of Strategic Studies from the U.S. Army War College, and an MBA from Cameron University. She currently chairs the advisory board of GCR Group, a global producer and marketer of critical minerals. Keravuori holds a directorship certification from NACD (NACD.DC) and is a Qualified Risk Director (QRD) through the DCRO Institute. She is also a member of Women Corporate Directors. “Rose’s extraordinary leadership experience, deep expertise in international security and risk management, and proven ability to navigate complex global environments make her an outstanding addition to our Board,” said TJ Kennedy, Chairman of the Board. “As Byrna expands across the consumer, professional security, and international markets, Rose’s strategic perspective will be invaluable in helping guide the Company through its next phase of growth. On behalf of the Board, I also want to thank Emily Rooney for her service and leadership contributions to Byrna over nearly five years.” “Over the course of my career, I have seen how preparation, sound judgment, and access to effective tools can make a meaningful difference in high-pressure situations,” Keravuori said. “Byrna’s mission to expand access to innovative, less-lethal personal security solutions strongly resonates with me. I am honored to join the Board and look forward to applying my experience in strategy, risk, and complex operations to support Byrna’s responsible growth and long-term success.” About Byrna Technologies Inc. Byrna is a personal defense technology company specializing in the development, manufacture, and sale of innovative less-lethal personal security solutions. For more information on the Company, please visit the corporate website here or the Company’s investor relations site here . The Company is the manufacturer of the Byrna® CL, Byrna® LE and Byrna® SD personal security devices, state-of-the-art handheld CO2 powered launchers designed to provide a less-lethal alternative to a firearm for the consumer, private security, and law enforcement markets. To purchase Byrna products, visit the Company’s e-commerce store. title: Gordon Murray Special Vehicles Previews Its Next Supercar
summary: After his Le Mans GTR reached a major milestone in France last month, renowned road- and race-car designer Gordon Murray is headed to Monterey Car Week in California to unveil a new car. The model was designed by his company’s Special Vehicles division, so it should be even more extreme than the already high-performance cars […]
body_text: After his Le Mans GTR reached a major milestone in France last month, renowned road- and race-car designer Gordon Murray is headed to Monterey Car Week in California to unveil a new car. The model was designed by his company’s Special Vehicles division, so it should be even more extreme than the already high-performance cars built by the boutique English brand. The preview image released by Gordon Murray Automotive (GMA) prompts more questions than answers. We see the outline of a car that has the proportions we associate with an engine mounted in the middle. The nose is low and the front overhang is short, while the back end looks big enough to house an engine. None of the styling cues are familiar, so odds are this is a new car rather than an evolution of an existing one. One detail that immediately stands out is the relatively subtle styling. There’s a NACA duct on the doors and a roof-mounted scoop, but the latest Special Vehicles model steers clear of wings, flared wheel arches, and other track-inspired aero parts adopted by other GMA vehicles . Indianapolis 500 and Le Mans winner Dario Franchitti, who helps Gordon Murray Automotive fine-tune its cars, will introduce the new model. The car will be the centerpiece in a display of vehicles that will include customer-owned T.50 models and the Le Mans GTR. Gordon Murray will unveil the yet-unnamed new model at The Quail on Friday, August 14, at 11:45 a.m. local time. It may be too late to buy one if you haven’t already been assigned a build slot: Production will undoubtedly be limited, and the company proudly pointed out that every vehicle it has announced so far is sold out. We wouldn’t be surprised if this model is, too. The post Gordon Murray Special Vehicles Previews Its Next Supercar appeared first on Hagerty Media .

title: Top Cold Email Services in 2026 (Best Agencies & Tools Compared)
summary: Discover the best cold email services in 2026. Compare Cleverly, Smartlead, Hypergen, Skrapp, Aerosend, Dripify, and LaGrowthMachine, plus learn how to choose the right solution for outbound growth.
body_text: What are the best cold email services in 2026? Short answer: The best cold email services in 2026 are Skrapp, Cleverly, Smartlead, Hypergen, Aerosend, Dripify, and LaGrowthMachine. Some are done-for-you outbound services, while others are software platforms that help internal teams run cold email at scale. The best choice depends on whether you need full execution, lead sourcing, email deliverability infrastructure , LinkedIn automation, or multi-channel outbound. TL;DR Skrapp → best for email finding and lead enrichment Smartlead → best for scaling cold email campaigns Hypergen → best for outbound + RevOps + systems Cleverly → best done-for-you cold email service Aerosend → best for deliverability infrastructure Dripify → best for LinkedIn-first outreach LaGrowthMachine → best for multi-channel outbound What is a cold email service? A cold email service is any solution that helps businesses find prospects, launch outreach campaigns, improve inbox placement, and generate meetings or revenue through outbound email. In practice, “cold email service” is a broader and more accurate term than “agency” because the market now includes both service providers and software platforms. Some companies handle everything for you, while others provide the infrastructure, data, automation, and workflow tools your team needs to run outbound internally. The two types of cold email services 1. Done-for-you cold email services These companies handle campaign setup, targeting, messaging, and execution for you. 2. Cold email platforms These tools give your team the software needed to manage prospecting, sending, automation, or deliverability internally. Both can work extremely well. The right choice depends on your team, your budget, and your growth stage. Comparison of the best cold email services Rank Service Type Best for Main strength 1 Skrapp Platform Lead sourcing Email finding + enrichment 2 Smartlead Platform Scaling outbound Deliverability + infrastructure 3 Hypergen Service B2B outbound systems Execution + RevOps 4 Cleverly Platform Outsourced outbound Fully managed campaigns 5 Aerosend Platform Deliverability Inbox placement control 6 Dripify Platform LinkedIn outreach Automation + team workflows 7 LaGrowthMachine Platform Multi-channel outreach Unified workflows Cold email services comparison by use case Use case Best service Why Done-for-you lead generation Cleverly Fully managed outbound campaigns with clear service packaging Scaling cold email campaigns Smartlead Built for multi-inbox, multi-domain outbound B2B outbound + RevOps Hypergen Combines outreach execution with systems and deliverability support LinkedIn-first outreach Dripify Strong LinkedIn automation and agency workflows Deliverability and inbox placement Aerosend Infrastructure-first approach to outbound Email finding and enrichment Skrapp Helps teams find and verify business emails quickly Multi-channel outbound LaGrowthMachine Combines email, LinkedIn, X, and calls In practice, many teams combine several services rather than relying on one tool. A common stack is to use Skrapp for lead sourcing, Smartlead for sending and automation, and a deliverability-focused layer to improve inbox placement before scaling volume. Best Cold Email Services in 2026 1. Skrapp - Best Cold Email Service for Email Finding and Enrichment Best for: teams that need verified business emails and lead enrichment before launching outreach. Skrapp deserves a place in this ranking because lead sourcing is one of the most important parts of cold email success. The platform positions itself as a lead search and enrichment tool that helps users find business emails, verify leads, and expand outreach. It also says it is trusted by 2M+ professionals, and its email finder page claims up to 92% accuracy for professional email lookups by name and company. That makes Skrapp highly relevant for founders, SDR teams, agencies, and outbound operators who need a reliable way to build prospect lists before those contacts ever enter a sequencing tool. Skrapp is not a sending platform in the same sense as Smartlead or LaGrowthMachine, which is exactly why it is useful. It solves an earlier step in the outbound workflow: finding and enriching the right contacts. If list quality is your bottleneck, Skrapp can add more value than another sequencing tool. It is particularly useful for LinkedIn-based prospecting workflows and teams that want a lighter, more specialized option for email discovery and enrichment before handing leads off to their outreach system. Key features Business email finder Lead enrichment Email verification support LinkedIn-oriented prospect sourcing Pros Strong fit for list building Useful before outreach starts Easy to combine with sending platforms Cons Not a full outreach automation tool Best used as part of a broader outbound stack 2. Smartlead - Best Cold Email Service for Scaling Campaigns Best for: agencies and internal teams that need to scale outbound safely across multiple inboxes and domains. Smartlead ranks second because it has become one of the clearest software choices for high-volume cold email with a strong deliverability angle. Its official positioning centers on AI outbound and deliverability infrastructure, and it says it is trusted by 100,000+ businesses ranging from agencies to Fortune 500 companies. Smartlead is especially useful when the real challenge is not just writing emails, but managing multiple sending accounts, protecting account health, and keeping campaigns scalable. For operators focused on scale, workflow, and infrastructure, Smartlead is one of the strongest platforms on the market. Saleshandy - Best Cold Email Service for All-in-One Outbound Best for: sales teams, agencies, and founders who want lead sourcing, deliverability, and campaign automation without stitching together three separate tools. Saleshandy earns a place in this ranking because it solves a problem most outbound stacks quietly ignore: the cost and friction of running lead sourcing, sending infrastructure, and deliverability through different platforms. Most operators end up paying separately for a database, a sequencing tool, and a warmup layer. Saleshandy puts all three inside one workflow, starting at $25 per month with no per-seat fees and no restrictions on email accounts. For a five-person team, that compares directly to $395 or more on platforms that charge per user for the same functionality. The deliverability side is where Saleshandy stands apart from generic sequencers. It includes an Inbox Placement Test that shows where emails land across Gmail, Outlook, and Yahoo before a campaign goes out; unlimited email warm-up; sender rotation across all connected accounts; and sequence scoring that flags issues before they affect inbox placement. On the prospecting side, the platform includes an 852M+ B2B contact database with 75+ filters and an AI lead finder that works from natural language prompts. An AI Sequence Copilot builds complete multi-step campaigns from a website URL and ICP details in minutes. Replies are managed through a unified inbox with AI sentiment sorting, and a built-in Kanban CRM handles pipeline tracking without leaving the platform. Hypergen - Best Cold Email Service for Outbound + RevOps Best for: SaaS companies, M&A firms, marketing agencies, and service businesses that want outbound execution plus strong internal systems. Hypergen stands out because it is not just running cold email campaigns; it is building a broader outbound engine around them. According to the company materials you shared, campaigns typically launch within about three weeks and are built to avoid breaking deliverability or internal processes as teams scale. That makes Hypergen one of the strongest choices for businesses that want outbound tied closely to operations and revenue systems, not just meetings on the calendar. Cleverly - Best Done-for-You Cold Email Service Best for: businesses that want meetings booked without building and managing their own outbound team. Cleverly is the strongest pure service-led choice in this ranking because it clearly positions itself as a B2B lead generation agency and handles outreach execution for clients. The company runs campaigns across LinkedIn, cold email, and cold calling, and highlights scale metrics such as 224.7K leads generated, $312M in pipeline, and $51.2M in revenue generated on its site. That combination of managed execution, proof, and broad outbound capability makes Cleverly one of the best cold email services for businesses that want results without becoming operators themselves. Aerosend - Best Cold Email Service for Deliverability Best for: outbound teams that see deliverability as the real constraint in growth. Its site emphasizes high-deliverability email, improved inbox placement, and sender reputation, while its agency-focused resources talk about dedicated infrastructure, dynamic IP rotation, and domain burn alerts. That focus makes Aerosend particularly relevant for operators who already understand that cold email performance is heavily influenced by infrastructure and account health, not just copy and sequence logic. For many teams, Aerosend is not the tool that writes copy or builds the lead list. It is the service that helps preserve inbox placement and campaign stability. It is particularly useful for founder-led sales, B2B teams, and agencies looking for a broader outbound operating system rather than a narrow sender. LaGrowthMachine is strongest when used by teams that already understand their ICP and want to coordinate multiple channels cleanly. It requires more strategy than a simple email sender, but that complexity can be an advantage when single-channel outreach is too easy for prospects to ignore. Key features Multi-channel automation Unified inbox Email + LinkedIn + X + calls workflows Pros Diversifies outbound touchpoints Good fit for modern B2B prospecting Useful for multi-touch campaigns Cons More complex than email-only tools Honorable mentions A few tools are also worth considering even though they are outside your preferred top-7 ranking: Instantly for ease of use and quick campaign launch Apollo for combining prospect data and outreach in one platform Lemlist for personalization-led outreach and creative campaign assets Reply.io for structured SDR workflows and sales automation What is the best cold email service overall? If you want a fully outsourced growth partner, Cleverly is the strongest choice in this ranking. If you want the best platform for scaling outbound yourself, Smartlead is the strongest overall software pick. If you want a more systems-driven service partner that blends execution with RevOps and infrastructure, Hypergen is an excellent fit. And if your main problem is list quality or inbox placement, Skrapp and Aerosend can solve problems that generic outreach tools often ignore. Why deliverability is the foundation of cold email Cold email success depends on sender reputation and inbox placement. Domain health, authentication, engagement signals, and sending behavior all influence whether a campaign lands in the inbox or vanishes into spam. That is why deliverability is no longer a technical detail to fix later. It is the foundation that determines whether copywriting, targeting, and sequencing can work at all. Even the best service provider or platform will underperform if the setup is weak. The role of email warmup in cold email success Most cold email tools focus on sending, workflow, and prospecting. Email warmup solves a different problem: building sender reputation gradually so campaigns can scale more safely. Warmup helps increase sending volume over time, generates positive engagement signals, and supports more stable inbox placement . That is why many serious outbound teams do not rely on a single tool alone. They combine list building, outreach, and deliverability layers to improve performance. This is also why many teams pair a sending platform with a dedicated warmup and deliverability solution like Mailwarm to improve inbox placement before scaling. How to choose the right cold email service Choose a done-for-you service if: You want meetings booked for you You do not want to manage outbound internally You value speed and simplicity over direct control You are early-stage or bandwidth-constrained Choose a platform if: You want more control over campaigns You already have founders, SDRs, or operators running outbound You want to optimize long-term tooling costs You need flexibility to test and scale internally Key decision criteria Deliverability capabilities Ease of use Scalability Multi-channel support Prospect data access Workflow complexity Pricing and ROI potential Final insight The biggest mistake people make in 2026 is still thinking cold email is mainly about sending software. It is not. The real winners treat outbound as a system: lead sourcing, targeting, infrastructure, copy, workflow, reputation, and follow-up all working together. That is why the best cold email service is rarely the one with the most features. It is the one that solves your actual bottleneck. If you need execution, a managed service like Cleverly or Hypergen can move faster than a DIY stack. If you need scale, Smartlead is stronger. If your real issue is prospect data, Skrapp can be more valuable than another sequencer. If deliverability is what is holding performance back, Aerosend and a dedicated warmup layer matter more than another automation feature. So the authority view is simple: cold email in 2026 is no longer a tool-first decision. It is a systems decision. The teams that win are the ones that choose the right service model, protect deliverability early, and build an outbound process that can scale without collapsing. That is where a sustainable pipeline is created - and that is what separates serious outbound operators from everyone else. FAQ What is a cold email service? A cold email service is any solution that helps a business source prospects, send outreach, improve inbox placement, and generate meetings or revenue through outbound email. It can be a managed service or a software platform. What is the best cold email service for outsourced outbound? For outsourced outbound, Cleverly is the clearest fit in this ranking because it is positioned as a full-service lead generation agency rather than a software tool. What is the best cold email platform for scale? For scale, Smartlead is one of the strongest choices because it is built around multi-account outbound and deliverability infrastructure. What is the best tool for finding business emails? Skrapp is one of the strongest options in this list for email finding and enrichment, especially when lead sourcing is the bottleneck before outreach starts. Why do cold emails go to spam? Cold emails usually go to spam because of weak sender reputation, poor infrastructure, missing authentication, low engagement, or overly aggressive sending patterns. Is cold email still effective in 2026? Yes. Cold email is still effective in 2026, but low-quality mass outreach is much less effective than it used to be. Personalized, targeted, and well-delivered campaigns still work. What matters most in cold email success? The biggest factors are:- deliverability- targeting- messaging- consistencyIf emails do not reach the inbox, the rest matters far less. Do you need email warmup for cold email? In most cases, yes. Warmup is especially important for new domains, new inboxes, or teams planning to scale outbound seriously.

title: Games Like Shift at Midnight: 7 Skinwalker and Anomaly Horror Games to Play Next
summary: Finished Shift at Midnight? Here are 7 games like it - skinwalker spotting, ID checking and anomaly horror - starting with a free browser one you can play now.
body_text: Shift at Midnight took a very old horror idea - something is pretending to be a person - and attached it to the most mundane job imaginable. You are behind a gas station counter at 3am, you have an ID in your hand, and you have to decide. It is short, it is cheap, and once you have cleared it you will want more of exactly that feeling. Here are seven games like Shift at Midnight, starting with one you can play free in your browser in the next thirty seconds. 1. Six Midnight Shifts (free, in your browser) The closest free match, and the only one on this list built specifically around the same loop: convenience store, night shift, customers who may not be human. You serve the queue, maintain the store, cross-check faces and answers against county records, and keep a sidearm under the counter for the moment you are certain. Six shifts, single-player, no download. Play Six Midnight Shifts free - browser-based, desktop and mobile. More on it in our free-to-play guide . 2. That's Not My Neighbor The doppelganger game that walked so Shift at Midnight could run. You are a 1955 apartment doorman checking IDs against a bulletin of known impostors, and the tells are tiny: a wrong eye colour, a name spelled almost right. If the verification part of Shift at Midnight is what hooked you, start here. 3. Papers, Please The origin point of the whole genre. No monsters, just documents, contradictions and a moral cost to every stamp. It is the game that proved a desk job could be the tensest thing on your hard drive. 4. Phasmophobia Co-op investigation horror with proximity chat, where the fun is four people in a dark house disagreeing about evidence. There is even an official Shift at Midnight x Phasmophobia bundle on Steam, which tells you how closely the two audiences overlap. 5. Lethal Company The modern co-op horror standard: quotas, scrap, proximity chat, and friends dying stupidly. Different job, identical group dynamic - the shared shift where somebody is definitely about to make a bad call. 6. I'm on Observation Duty Pure anomaly spotting. You watch security cameras and report what changed: a chair moved, a painting turned, a figure that was not in that corner a minute ago. It trains exactly the muscle Shift at Midnight tests when something in your store is subtly wrong. 7. Night of the Consumers Retail horror at its most literal. You are a supermarket employee, the customers are relentless and inhuman in a very different way, and the whole thing is a panic attack about service work. It is the comedy sibling to Shift at Midnight's dread. Or make your own Six Midnight Shifts was built with Rosebud AI by describing the game in plain English. If none of the seven above is quite the skinwalker game in your head, read How to Make Your Own Shift at Midnight-Style Game and build it instead. Frequently asked questions What game is most similar to Shift at Midnight? That's Not My Neighbor is the closest paid game for the identity-verification loop. Six Midnight Shifts is the closest free one, and the only browser game built around the same convenience store night shift premise. Is there a free game like Shift at Midnight? Yes - Six Midnight Shifts is free in the browser, and Shift at Midnight itself has a free multiplayer demo on Steam. Are these games co-op? Phasmophobia and Lethal Company are co-op focused. That's Not My Neighbor, Papers Please, I'm on Observation Duty and Six Midnight Shifts are single-player. title: The Best Subcompact SUVs of 2026
summary: Subcompact SUVs provide an excellent combination of comfort, capability, safety, and efficiency, all with a budget-friendly price. With practically every leading automaker offering an option in this segment, we've compiled a list of standout options.
body_text: It’s no wonder subcompact SUVs are the fastest-growing segment of the new car market. They offer an excellent mix of comfort, capability, safety, and efficiency at a price that most can afford. In this segment, drivers get a higher seating position and more functional space than they would in a sedan, and some models are even respectably good at driving off-road. The subcompact SUV market is so popular that nearly every major automaker now offers at least one. These vehicles often feature cutting-edge infotainment tech and the most up-to-date advanced safety features. To help you make sense of it all, we’ve assembled a list of the best SUVs in the segment. Subaru Crosstrek CarGurus expert rating: 8 out of 10 CarGurus user rating: 4.6 out of 5 Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus: 31.4% Overall CarGurus rating: 4.6 out of 5 Pros Cons Standard all-wheel drive Underwhelming base engine Impressive technology Interior materials feel cheap Outstanding off-road capability in Wilderness trim To create the Crosstrek Wilderness, Subaru took its best-selling subcompact crossover and gave it a serious boost in capability for adventure seekers. With its signature rugged styling, lifted 9.3-inch ground clearance, and a ladder-style roof rack rated for 700 pounds of static load, the Crosstrek Wilderness is ready for everything from weekend camping trips to muddy trailheads. Inside, StarTex synthetic leather upholstery is easy to clean and largely waterproof, while all-weather floor mats and additional trunk cupholders make it a practical partner for outdoor lifestyles. The upgraded 2.5-liter flat-four engine produces 182 hp and 178 lb-ft of torque, paired with a CVT tuned for off-road use and a robust X-Mode traction system—making sure the Crosstrek Wilderness feels just as confident off the beaten path as it does on your daily commute. Despite its tougher persona, the Crosstrek Wilderness doesn't forget everyday usability. It features a large 11.6-inch touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with Subaru's acclaimed EyeSight safety suite offering adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, and automatic emergency braking. While cargo space behind the rear seats is a bit modest at 19.9 cubic feet, folding the seats opens up a generous 54.7 cubic feet—enough for gear, groceries, or even a weekend's worth of camping supplies. With a starting price that includes AWD (unlike many competitors), strong resale value, and a user-friendly, adventure-ready interior, the Crosstrek Wilderness stands out as a go-anywhere, do-anything subcompact SUV for active drivers. title: Language Access in Palliative Care: What the Data Shows
summary: Language barriers in palliative care cause consent errors and worse outcomes for LEP patients. See the data and how to close the gaps. July 2026.
body_text: If your team treats language access as an occasional accommodation instead of a standing clinical requirement, the outcomes data from palliative care should change that view. Patients with language barriers are less likely to complete advance directives, less likely to enroll in hospice, and more likely to receive care at the end of life that doesn't reflect what they actually wanted. Here's where those gaps come from and what closes them. TLDR: Over 22% of U.S. residents speak a non-English language at home, making LEP patients a standing feature of your palliative census. Language barriers push LEP patients toward more aggressive end-of-life care, not less, because goals-of-care conversations fail before consent is reached. Misheard DNR discussions become documentation and consent problems; what gets signed may not reflect what the patient wanted. 54% of hospice bereavement coordinators report needing more interpreter services for LEP families, and most lack the tools to deliver grief care. Opalite Health is a physician-led AI medical interpreter built for goals-of-care and end-of-life discussions, validated in an independent study with Johns Hopkins Medicine. Why language barriers at end of life carry higher stakes A daughter sits beside her father's bed. The physician is trying to explain that further chemotherapy will not help, and that the goal now is comfort. The words that carry that message have to be exact. Get one of them wrong, and the family may hear abandonment instead of care. Routine visits forgive small slips. A missed word during a medication refill rarely changes the outcome. End-of-life conversations work differently. These discussions ask patients and families to weigh prognosis, decide what a good death looks like, and consent to comfort-focused treatment. Each one demands precise wording and emotional attunement at once. When someone speaks a language other than English, that precision breaks down first. The scale of language barriers in U.S. healthcare Language access is a systemic feature of American healthcare. More than 22% of people aged five or older speak a language other than English at home, with Spanish being the most common. Serious illness does not sort patients by the language they speak. As the country grows more linguistically diverse, a rising share of people entering palliative and hospice care will have limited English proficiency. For anyone leading clinical operations or health equity work, that reframes the problem. This is a standing feature of your patient population, not an occasional exception at the bedside. How language discordance shapes the palliative care experience Pull the research together and a pattern shows up quickly. Across different study designs and viewpoints, language discordance carries a negative impact on the quality and accessibility of palliative, end-of-life, and hospice care. The effect is not confined to one moment in the visit. Patients with a non-English language preference frequently face health equity disparities for LEP patients in communication, symptom management, and care transitions. The gap follows them from the first conversation about goals through the handoffs between settings, and each stage compounds the last. The sections that follow trace where those breakdowns land, one clinical consequence at a time. Symptom assessment and pain control gaps for LEP patients Pain is where the gap gets dangerous. When professional interpreters were absent, patients with limited English proficiency reported worse pain and worse non-pain symptom management. Their family members lacked a clear grasp of the clinical picture, including prognosis and diagnosis, and carried more stress about events at the bedside. Presence of an interpreter is only half the story. A 2015 systematic review (Hultsjö & Hjelm) found a direct link between interpreter type and care quality across every study reviewed. A hurried phone interpreter service , an untrained family member, and a trained medical interpreter do not produce the same result. Who bridges the language gap shapes whether a patient's pain gets named, measured, and treated. [@portabletext/react] Unknown block type "table", specify a component for it in the `components.types` prop Language barriers in advance care planning and goals-of-care conversations Advance care planning is a series of decisions, each one recorded. A prognosis gets explained. A patient chooses whether to accept resuscitation. Someone is named to speak when the patient no longer can. Goals of care get written into the chart. Every step turns a spoken exchange into a legal document, so the words on both sides have to land accurately. That is where the gap becomes a liability. Patients with limited English proficiency experience disparities in end-of-life decision making and advance care planning. Read that as a documentation and consent problem. If a DNR discussion is misheard, what ends up signed may not reflect what the patient actually wanted. When language gaps lead to more aggressive, less aligned care Here is the finding that surprises most people. Language barriers do not push patients toward less treatment at the end of life. They push toward more. The evidence suggests that LEP patients receive more aggressive care toward the end of life. In the ICU, patients with limited English proficiency were less likely to change to a do-not-resuscitate code status. The mechanism is the missing conversation. When a goals-of-care discussion cannot happen accurately, no one confirms what the patient would refuse. So the default takes over, and the default is intervention. Machines stay on. Codes stay full. Language barriers in hospice enrollment and bereavement access Hospice enrollment is the last handoff, and it stalls when language gets in the way. Getting there depends on a family grasping the prognosis, choosing comfort over cure, and clearing a consent process thick with paperwork. Each step needs accurate interpretation. One study showed that language barriers for Spanish-speaking patients influenced their access to hospice, particularly bereavement care after death. The barrier does not lift once the patient dies. Grief support has to reach families in a language they understand, and often it does not. In one systematic review , 54% of hospice bereavement coordinators said more interpreter services were needed for LEP families. More than half lacked the tools to deliver grief care. The role and limits of professional interpreters in palliative care Professional medical interpreters are the recognized standard, and for good reason. A trained interpreter brings clinical vocabulary, cultural intelligence in medical interpretation , and a commitment to conveying what was actually said. In serious illness, that skill carries real weight. The setting also creates strain that routine visits do not. Interpreters can struggle in palliative care discussions, while family members pressed into the role risk ethical dilemmas that compromise accuracy and the patient's own voice. None of this is a knock on interpreters. It explains why palliative interpretation needs its own training, support, and reliable access. Practical strategies for improving language access in palliative care settings Language access at end of life works best when it is built in ahead of the conversation, not summoned mid-crisis. A few moves matter most: Train interpreters in palliative terminology and emotional support, beyond clinical vocabulary alone. Embed language access into clinical workflows for advance care planning and every care transition, including hospice intake and discharge. Prepare plain language patient-facing materials for consent, discharge, and bereavement. Set escalation policies for high-stakes talks like DNR and goals of care. Document every interpreted encounter, including interpreter type, for quality and compliance review. How Opalite Health supports language access in serious illness care Opalite Health is a physician-led AI interpreter for healthcare built for real clinical communication, including goals-of-care and end-of-life discussions where precise wording directly affects what patients consent to. It provides real-time interpretation across more than 150 languages and dialects, operates under HIPAA-compliant workflows with Business Associate Agreements available, and integrates with leading EHRs including Epic, Cerner, and eClinicalWorks. The design is healthcare-specific. Opalite handles clinical terminology, medication instructions, and consent language, not general consumer phrasing. Opalite Guardian, our quality framework, applies automated and human-supported controls to reduce clinically meaningful interpretation errors. That accuracy has been measured. In an independent validation study with Johns Hopkins Medicine, Opalite produced more than 90% fewer major and critical errors compared with certified medical interpreters. When one misheard word can commit a patient to care they never wanted, that margin counts. For high-risk palliative encounters, Opalite works within a risk-based language access framework alongside qualified human interpreters, never in place of them. See CIFC Health's instant interpretation case study . Final thoughts on language access and end-of-life care quality What the research shows is a consistent, avoidable pattern: patients who cannot communicate in English receive less aligned care, more unwanted intervention, and less access to hospice and grief support. That is a care quality issue and a consent issue, and it sits inside your operations. Each gap traced here has a clinical fix. See Opalite Health in palliative care .
